The key sits on the desk leather. Brass. Small teeth. No inn tag. Lamp oil, river water, and a quiet that isn't empty.
File the night. The key stays put. I have closed a case on less — and been wrong in a way ink doesn't show.
Work the morning. If the gray overcoat comes for the key, he can wait in the wet like the rest of the city. I am done calling coats an ending.
Come in out of the wet. Tell me what the city already knows.
Sit down. Three nights past: last place, last word, last soul who saw her.
Convince me she didn't buy a room and a new name.
My sister Lillian vanished three nights past. Not left. Not fled. The lamps were still lit. The kettle still held heat. Her hush-ward didn't trip. It trips for the post.
Mr. Voss? Forgive the hour. They told me the night porter only takes living errands after dawn.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.key.revea: Since I found it, a man has been following me. Gray overcoat. Black gloves. He waits across from my lodgings and turns away when I look, like a man embarrassed for us both. The streetlamps dim when he stands under them.

Sewn into the lining: a brass key. Small. Old teeth. No inn tag. It hummed once against my palm and went quiet. Lillian still sews her own hems. She would not leave a coat that cost her a week — or a key that cost her more.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.plea.b.te: If the gray overcoat comes for the key, don't give it to him. I hired you to find my sister. Not to tidy up after someone else's ritual.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.plea.text: Please find her, Mr. Voss. Find the sister — not the coat's alibi.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.police.st: I asked for the night sergeant's notes. He offered tea and the speech he saves for drownings: tides, and "what the river keeps." I asked who benefited if Lillian stopped reading manifests. He stopped offering tea.

The Watch filed it soft: a woman gone, no struggle, coat recovered, probable drowning. Case cooling before the ink dried. They were polite. It's cheaper than looking. They did not offer the file — or the reading-rights on it.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.reply.cyn: Lillian hated the river. She hated an unfinished book more. The Watch found her coat and called it an ending. Endings file faster. I put my hands in the lining.
If she had a clean alibi I would not be dripping on your floor.
Fine. Mark your coin. Look at the coat first. Whoever emptied it left the key — and meant you to.
At least you're honest about the price.
I'll take the key. I'll take the case. Don't wait on a raven — or the hush-charm on the sill.
You'll take it. That's enough. You get the key.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.reply.goo: She worked late at the shipping office near Wharf Ladder — ledgers, manifests, seals that bite if you read them wrong. Never late for the ferry. The ferry often was. Tuesday night she left at nine. By midnight the river had her coat.
Thank you. Two hundred now — good coin, not dock-ledger chalk. The rest when you find her.
The pockets were turned inside out — careful work, not panic.
I'll take the key. I'll take the case. Don't wait on a raven — or the hush-charm on the sill.
The follower: tall, hat brim low, gloves that stay on. He never crosses the street. He only makes sure I know it's his.
I'll take the promise. I'll walk carefully.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.reply.neu: Last confirmed: Wharf Ladder shipping office, Tuesday, nine. She told a clerk she had one more errand in the upper city. No name. No hired coach chalked on the desk slate. Midnight, the river watch found her coat below the old iron stairs — empty. Arranged. Folded neater than their report. Like an offering someone wanted found.
They handed the coat back in a paper wrap. I took it home and found the key they never felt for.
That's the work I came to buy — river stones, duty roster, the shipping-office clock that runs three minutes fast when the night crew wants an alibi the wards will swear to.
I'll take the key. I'll take the case. Don't wait on a raven — or the hush-charm on the sill.
I'll stay with a friend on Printers' Quarter tonight. Real locks. A threshold that holds. Fewer witnesses who owe the docks a favor.

Gray overcoat, black gloves, no limp, no badge. Bakery doorway across from my stairs, eleven to one. He buys nothing. When a cart rattles past, he uses the noise to move. Professional habits — or something wearing them.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.reply.pre: I'll take the key. I'll take the case. Don't wait on a raven — or the hush-charm on the sill.
Fine. Lillian was reading manifests. I don't have the names clean enough for a magistrate's hall. I have a sister and a key.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.triad.key: Describe the follower once more, then go somewhere with a real lock — and a threshold that holds.
If anyone asks, I never saw a key.
Tell me what you're still not saying. What did Lillian find in those manifests?

I'm leaving the key if you'll take the case. Two hundred now. The rest when you find her.

Tell me how you want to play this.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.triad.pol: I pull the file they won't show you.
The drowning's too tidy. I'll hear how they blessed it.
I'll tell the night sergeant I believe him. See who relaxes.
The Watch has a drowning, filed and dried. I have a sister. What do you do with that?
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.voss.monologue: Rain had been working the glass since afternoon. The ward on the sill hadn't bothered to argue.
Three unpaid notices. Same name on every one. Coin that never quite warmed in the hand.
Hearth ticks. Timbers arguing in the walls. Rain on the glass, filing its usual complaint. Same as yesterday — and the night I closed a file clean.

I told myself I was done with vanishings after Pell Street. The rent — and whatever listens for rent in this building — said otherwise.

Then the hallway. Heels on tired boards. A pause outside the door, like someone testing a threshold. Like someone who had already been told the river was answer enough.

A woman out of the rain. A coat that remembered a body and had forgotten the rest.

The door opened. I already hated how familiar that shape felt.
The key sits on the desk leather. Brass. Small teeth. No inn tag. Lamp oil, river water, and a quiet that isn't empty.
Three cold cases, two debts the ledger still remembers, and a clean page under the quill that hasn't learned a name yet.
The hall smelled worse — damp wool, old wards, someone else's business. At least it led somewhere.
strings.dlg.inspect.office.files.node.inspection: Sealed. Abandoned. And one folio I still lied about — to the client, and to whatever keeps the cabinet shut.
strings.dlg.inspect.office.phone.node.inspection: Empty iron perch. Droppings on the desk-leather edge. For once the bird had the decency to stay gone — and look guilty doing it.
strings.dlg.inspect.office.window.node.inspectio: Same rain, same glass. Now I had a client — and a key that hummed when the weather turned.
The rain had been working the glass longer than I had. The sill-ward didn't care either way.
strings.dlg.journal.chrono.client-retained: Retained by Lila March. The Empty Coat is open.
strings.dlg.journal.chrono.pressed-hard: Pushed Lila on what the Watch finished too early. Manifests.
strings.dlg.journal.chrono.wharf-ladder.last-shi: Wharf Ladder: Lillian left on Tuesday at nine. One more errand in the upper city. No coach on the desk slate.
strings.dlg.journal.lead.wharf-ladder.lost-crate: Merrick started to name a crate mark from the lost-crate lane, saw the quay, and stopped. Dock Authority keeps the lost-crate numbers.
strings.dlg.journal.lead.wharf-ladder.night-cloc: Wharf Ladder's night clock runs three minutes fast when the night crew wants an alibi. Somebody sets it. Clocks don't volunteer.
strings.dlg.journal.lead.wharf-ladder.reading-ri: Someone from Civic scrubbed the reading-rights on Lillian's last manifest pull after she vanished. Politely. Civic Spine keeps the records.
strings.dlg.journal.lead.wharf-ladder.tallow-sta: Ketch and Bram were told to burn the March folio. The gray gent pays at the Tallow Stair.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.aftermath.cost.cho: Two marks in the night book now. The Watch-house will start closing doors.
Leave by the dark side of the quay. There's no shortage.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.aftermath.cost.tex: Lamps were coming along the quay. Dock Authority night-men, the kind who count heads before reasons. By morning the Watch would have my name for brawling at Wharf Ladder, in ink for once. Merrick was gone. So was any chance he'd say it twice.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.aftermath.lost.b.t: Nine o'clock. One more errand in the upper city. A slate nobody wrote on. And the river stones, where somebody had arranged a coat.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.aftermath.lost.cho: Get up. Slowly. Count what's still true.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.aftermath.lost.tex: I woke on the quay boards with rain in one ear and my pockets lighter. Whatever I'd taken off her desk had been taken back, or burned. The boards weren't saying.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.aftermath.tally.te: A chalk pay tally. Somebody's wages in somebody's hand, and a crate mark in the corner. The first thing tonight that tied the gray gent's money to a lost crate.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.aftermath.won.text: When it was over, the floor was mine and nobody wanted it. Ketch went down like freight off a bad crane. Bram held his knife like a pen and ran out of courage before he ran out of room.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.bram.overheard.tex: All of it? Even the bit that bites?
Three minutes fast. Somebody winds that clock with an opinion.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.desk.clock.text: The ferry horn went for the hour. The night clock was already three minutes past it, and looked pleased with itself.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.desk.edge.choice.0: Pocket it. Gently. It still looks hungry.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.desk.edge.text: A smear on the leather edge, brown as old tea, shaped like a glove that touched the wrong thing. Under the blotter, a scrap of seal-wax with the mark still sharp. The second check, or what was left of it.
Run a thumb along the desk-leather edge.
Wait for the ferry horn. Check the clock against it.
Merrick. Her last manifest pull. Where is it?
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.desk.hub.text: Lillian's desk. Ledgers squared to the edge. A pen laid parallel to the blotter, as if it expected an inspection. The kind of tidy that is either a habit or a warning.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.dry.after.text: They left the way weather leaves: not far. Merrick came out from behind the counter and found something urgent to file. The seal-room could wait until I had the rights to read it.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.e1.handoff.desk.te: Bram. Mind the lamp. Mr. Finder's leaving by the floor.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.e1.handoff.sealroo: Bell says somebody's asking. Seal-room's a bad place to be somebody.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.ketch.backoff.text: Does it. Then the Watch can have you. Paper keeps. Come on, Bram. Door's this way.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.ketch.callsbluff.c: Worth a try. Cheaper than silver.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.ketch.callsbluff.t: No, it doesn't. Nobody tells the Watch anything in this office. That's what the office is for.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.ketch.enter.choice: Step off? I've only just got comfortable.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.ketch.enter.text: Evening. We're here for paper, not for you. Step off the desk.
Time to leave by the door nobody paid to watch.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.ketch.overheard.te: Right. You heard the man. Burn the March folio. The gray gent pays at the Tallow Stair.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.ketch.who.text: Someone who pays in chalk and doesn't ask how it's spent. Desk, Mr. Finder.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.again.text: The hour's up, Mr. Voss. Come back with a new question or an old coin.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.bell.choic: Then I'd better find the back of this room.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.bell.text: I'm sorry. They pay me to be frightened of them first.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.bitten.tex: You opened it. Of course you opened it. Hold your hand up. You'll drip on the manifests.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.clock.text: By that one. Don't trust it. It runs three minutes fast when the night crew wants an alibi, and nobody asks me which nights.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.closed.tex: No. Not for silver, not for favours, not for you. Come back when you've got a clock that tells the truth.
Civic. Polite. Then nobody. Then everybody. Ask the lost-crate lane about the crates chalked with the—
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.desk.text: Her desk. I haven't touched it. I don't touch anything in here I'm not paid to. Touching is how this office bites.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.errand.tex: Upper city. She said it the way people say "the tooth-drawer." Somewhere you don't want to go, and go anyway.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.favour.tex: A finder who keeps quiet about clocks. They'll put you under glass at the Civic hall. Fine. A favour buys you the short version.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.ferry.text: She never missed the morning ferry. That night she did everything twice. Checked the seal, checked it again.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.greet.choi: Harlan Voss. I find people. I'm here about Lillian March.
Your other customer was first. I'll wait. I've nowhere drier to be.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.greet.text: Right. Well. We're shut. Unless you're the Watch, and you're not the Watch. The Watch wipes its feet.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.paid.text: That's more than the gray gent paid. He tips like a man buying rope. All right. Talk.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.price.choi: Fifty silver buys talk. More than whoever's paying you to be quiet.
No coin. A favour. Your clock stays your business. Nobody hears about it from me.
Here's my price. Talk, or Dock Authority hears you sell their silence twice.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.price.text: Everyone's here about Lillian March this week. Silence is a silver an hour, Mr. Voss. Talk is dearer, and it doesn't keep.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.sealroom.c: After she vanished. Who from Civic? Show me.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.sealroom.t: Her last pull's in the seal-room. Someone from Civic came for the reading-rights after. Polite. Wiped their feet, even. The folios still hurt if you touch the wrong line.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.shaken.cho: It had its say. I had mine.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.shaken.tex: You came out of the clock room. On your feet. Most people who go in there come out on somebody else's.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.slate.text: Nobody wipes that slate but me, and I didn't. It's clean because she never wrote on it. She walked. Or she went with somebody who doesn't need a slate.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.stall.choi: I'll wait at her desk. Take three.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.stall.text: The pull. Yes. It's filed. Under. Somewhere. Give me a minute. Minutes are cheap in here. We make our own.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.threat.tex: Dock Authority. You say it like it's a name, Mr. Voss. Down here it's weather. Fine. Fine. You'll get your talk.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.tuesday.ch: Did she say what the errand was?
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.tuesday.te: Tuesday she left at nine. Said she had one more errand in the upper city. No name. No coach, either. Look at the desk slate. Clean. Cleanest thing in the building.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.whisper.ch: Ring it. I'll be behind the wax. I want to hear what they're paid to say.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.merrick.whisper.te: Listen. They come at the bell. The gray gent's men. I'm paid to ring it if anyone asks about her folios. You paid more. I'm loyal like that. Back door's behind the presses.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.runner.hello.choic: River slips still logged by the bell, not the tide? I used to sign those.
Tell your night sergeant Harlan Voss is at Wharf Ladder tonight. He knows the name.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.runner.hello.text: Don't mind me. Night slips for the Watch-house. I carry paper. I don't read it. Reading's a different wage.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.runner.softfile.ch: Tell him Harlan Voss is at Wharf Ladder tonight. He'll sigh.
Mind the clock on your way out. It's keen.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.runner.softfile.te: River watch? Then you know the tide speech. The March coat's filed soft. The sergeant gave it the whole speech, tides and what the river keeps. He does it well. He's had practice.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.runner.told.choice: Two's a compliment. Now, clerk. Lillian March.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.runner.told.text: I'll tell him. He'll sigh. He sighs at most names. Yours might get two.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.sealroom.bite.text: The seal bit. Not hard. Hard enough to make its point, and draw a little blood to underline it. Out front, Merrick made the noise of a man watching his evening get worse.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.sealroom.folio.cho: Read the margin. Leave the seal alone.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.sealroom.folio.tex: The seal-room. Shelves of folios with wax on them like teeth. Her last pull sat on top. The reading-rights stamp had been scraped back to bare card. The seal under it was awake.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.sealroom.margin.te: The margin had carried a rights-line once. Now it carried a scratch where a name had been, neat as a clerk's apology. Whoever scrubbed it had manners, and a better pen than mine.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.voss.arrival.b.tex: The clock room was behind me now, quieter than when I'd gone in. Out front: brass seal-presses, an empty raven cage, a clock ticking like it had somewhere better to be. One clerk behind the counter, white as a fresh manifest. A Watch-house runner dripping on the mat.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.voss.arrival.choic: Leave Lila the dry side of the doorway.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.voss.arrival.text: Wharf Ladder after dark. The rain worked the tin roof harder than it ever bothered to on Sable Row. Lila's two hundred sat warm in my coat. Nothing else in it was. The key still hummed somewhere in my memory.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.voss.lila.text: Lila stayed outside, under a lintel with an old ward-mark that still held. She said she'd rather wait on a threshold she trusted than a clerk she didn't. Fair. I hadn't met him yet.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.voss.paid.text: Fifty silver. A quarter of Lila's two hundred, spent on one clerk's memory. I didn't ask for a receipt. He'd have charged for it.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.voss.quay.choice.1: Ring that and you'll need a new office.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.voss.quay.text: He stopped. His eyes went past me, through the window, to the quay. Under a lamp that had gone dim on purpose, a man in a gray overcoat shifted his weight. That was all. It was enough. Merrick's hand found the bell cord.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.warm.backdoor.choi: Look long enough to remember him.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.warm.backdoor.text: The back door let me out onto the quay. Across the water, under a lamp that had decided to be dim, a man in a gray overcoat stood very still. He didn't come closer. He didn't need to.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.warm.hide.text: I folded myself behind a shelf of wax that would have liked me dead. Merrick rang the bell like a man apologising to it. Boots came in. Two pairs. One heavy, one in a hurry.
strings.dlg.wharf-ladder.node.wharf.exit.text: Outside, the rain had found the tin roof again and was taking it personally. The river stones were next, where somebody had arranged a coat. Unless the gray overcoat had plans for tonight.
strings.dlg.inspect.office.perch.node.inspection: Empty iron perch. Droppings on the desk-leather edge. For once the bird had the decency to stay gone — and look guilty doing it.
strings.dlg.inspect.office.chest.node.inspection: Ward plans, old soundings, and streets that changed their names before their habits.
strings.dlg.inspect.office.lockbox.node.inspecti: A small lock for the things I could not afford to mislay.
strings.dlg.inspect.office.crates.node.inspectio: The cases nobody paid to have put in order.
strings.dlg.inspect.living.footlocker.node.inspe: Spare linen, old leather, and enough room for a better life.
strings.dlg.inspect.living.wardrobe.node.inspect: A coat for the rain. The rain never asked whether it was clean.
strings.dlg.inspect.living.bed.node.inspection.l: Sleep was available. Peace charged extra.
strings.dlg.inspect.living.washstand.node.inspec: Cold water and a towel worn thin enough to tell the truth.
strings.dlg.inspect.office.hearth.node.inspectio: The coals kept their own counsel.
